## `scripts/fp/traffic/ambient.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Ambient filler (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §6): unnamed commuters and pedestrians around the player, denser where sim.traffic and residents' trip_load are high (caps 40 cars, 60 people). The caps are spent where they can be seen: cars live within CAR_RING (just past VIS_CAR) and people within PED_RING (just past VIS_PERSON), both inside TRAFFIC_RADIUS. Cars appear and vanish only beyond MIN_SPAWN and out of the camera's view; people appear out of view beyond PED_MIN_SPAWN, or fade in (render.gd) far enough away that the fade is all one sees. A synchronous fill (first fill, load, teleport: the whole view is new) places agents anywhere outside the player's personal space. Also the curb parking that makes streets look lived in: deterministic per slot, so it never changes as the player walks.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `MAX_CARS = 40`
- `MAX_PEDS = 60`
- `CARS_PER_TILE = 0.3`: Cars per road tile within the ring, before congestion and trip load.
- `PEDS_PER_TILE = 1.6`
- `MIN_SPAWN = 6.0`
- `CAR_RING = 11.0`: Ambient cars live within this (VIS_CAR + 1, capped by TRAFFIC_RADIUS) and leave out of sight beyond it plus 0.5.
- `PED_RING = 4.8`: People are drawn only to VIS_PERSON, so ambient walkers live in a ring just past it: spawned out of view beyond PED_MIN_SPAWN (in view, fading in, beyond PED_FADE_SPAWN), removed beyond PED_RING + 0.7 out of sight.
- `PED_MIN_SPAWN = 2.0`
- `PED_FADE_SPAWN = 3.0`
- `PERSONAL = 2.5 * WS.M`: Nothing is ever placed this close to the player, even on a synchronous fill.
- `SYNC_CAR_CLEAR = 0.35`: A synchronous fill keeps cars at least this far from the camera (no car parked in one's face).
- `PARK_CHANCE = {D.ZONE_C: 0.55, D.ZONE_R: 0.45, D.ZONE_I: 0.25}`: Kerbside parking density by the lot beside the slot.
- `PARK_OTHER = 0.18`

### Properties

- `car_model: Callable`: Callables set by the feature: car_model(seed) -> int, person_model(seed) -> int, dims(model) -> Vector3, visible(pos) -> bool (inside the camera frustum and within car range).

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_lg: LG, p_sw: SW, p_vh: VH, p_wk: WK) -> void`
- `func refresh_tiles() -> void`: Re-reads the road tiles (after a lane rebuild).
- `func counts() -> Vector2i`
- `func targets(p: Vector3) -> Vector2i`: [target cars, target pedestrians] near p from road density, congestion and trip load.
- `func maintain(p: Vector3, fwd: Vector3, sync: bool) -> void`: Removes ambient agents beyond the radius (out of sight) and tops up toward the targets. sync: fill completely now (first fill or after a teleport), anywhere out of the camera's view.
- `func fill_parking() -> int`: Fills curb slots with parked cars, deterministically per slot (bulk: one lane rebuild after). Returns how many were parked.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/contact_shadows.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Contact shadows: a soft dark patch on the ground under every drawn vehicle and person, all in one MultiMesh draw. The sun's shadow maps reach only some of them (full and mid-LOD vehicles to render.SHADOW_DIST, people bodies to people.T1_NEAR, nothing after dark or under cloud), and without darkening where a body meets the road, a parked car or a walker seems to hover.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LIFT = 0.0015`: Height above the surface: clear of depth fighting with the road, too thin to see from the side.
- `CAR_PAD = Vector2(1.18, 1.08)`: Blob footprint against the body: vehicles a little wider and longer than their box, people a disc of PERSON_D.
- `PERSON_D = 0.7 * WS.M`
- `CAR_DARK = 0.62`: Darkness at the centre of the patch (0..1) and the patch's shape exponent (2 is an ellipse, larger is squarer: car bodies cover a rounded rectangle, feet an ellipse).
- `PERSON_DARK = 0.42`
- `CAR_SHAPE = 5.0`
- `PERSON_SHAPE = 2.0`
- `CAR_RANGE = 6.0`: Range, with a fade over the last FADE (vehicles beyond CAR_RANGE are a few pixels tall).
- `FADE = 0.6`
- `FLOATS = 16`
- `SHADER = """`

### Functions

- `func setup(root: Node3D) -> void`
- `func begin() -> void`
- `func car(p: Vector3, yaw: float, hw: float, l: float, d: float) -> void`: A vehicle of half width hw and length l at ground point p, heading yaw, d from the camera.
- `func person(p: Vector3, opacity: float) -> void`: A person standing at ground point p; opacity follows the body's own fade (0..1).
- `func finish() -> void`: Uploads this frame's patches (one buffer write).
- `func origin(k: int) -> Vector3`: Patch k's centre (tests).
- `func clear() -> void`

## `scripts/fp/traffic/fleets.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

City fleets on lanes in first person (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §5): buses on 2-4 seeded closed lines through the bus stops (they pull in at each shelter, people board and alight), delivery and garbage trucks, and emergency crews that run to incidents with sirens (through red lights at walking pace once the box is clear), wait at the scene, and drive back to the station. CityLife asks for vehicles through spawn_fleet / dispatch_crew; drivers are residents with the matching job when one is free, else "city crew".

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `DWELL = 9.0`
- `MAX_CREWS = 10`
- `ASTAR_PER_FRAME = 4`: Crew routes are A* builds: at most this many per frame (the feature refills the budget), the rest wait in `pending` (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §1).
- `CURB_LAT = 0.055`
- `JOBS = {"bus": "bus driver", "truck": "truck driver", "garbage_truck": "sanitation worker", "f...`

### Properties

- `stop_sides: Dictionary`: tile -> side index of its shelter
- `last_dispatch_fail: String`: Why the last crew build sent nobody ("" when it sent a crew); for tests and logs.
- `pending: Array`: Crew requests waiting for an A* slot: [kind, station, target]; crews waiting to route home.
- `astar_left: int`: A* builds left this frame.
- `retry_t: float`: Seconds before stale lines may be rebuilt again, and the current wait (it doubles while the rebuild keeps failing: a failed A* is the expensive case).

### Inner classes

- `Line`: A closed bus line: stops (tiles) in order, the lane beside each shelter and the legs between.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_f: Object, p_sim: CitySim, p_lg: LG, p_vh: VH) -> void`
- `func read_stops(view: CityView) -> Dictionary`: Shelter side of every bus stop (G1 may store it as a Vector2i; else inferred like CityView).
- `func stops_signature(view: CityView) -> String`: Signature of the stop set (lines rebuild when it changes).
- `func rebuild_lines(view: CityView) -> int`: Rebuilds the seeded lines from the current stops. Returns the number of lines.
- `func stale() -> bool`: True when the lines no longer match the roads: none although two stops exist (the roads between them may have been missing when the stops appeared), or a lane they use is gone.
- `func bus_choice(seq: Array[int], dest: int) -> Array`: [line id, board tile, alight tile] for a trip along road tiles seq to dest, or [].
- `func line(id: int) -> Line`
- `func count(role: String) -> int`
- `func fleet_size(kind: String) -> int`: Fleet size for CityLife's census (kind as CityLife names it).
- `func spawn_fleet(kind: String, start: Vector2i) -> void`: Adds one vehicle of a fleet (CityLife.external.spawn_fleet).
- `func dispatch_crew(kind: String, station: Vector2i, target: Vector2i) -> void`: Queues a crew (CityLife.external.dispatch_crew); it leaves when an A* slot is free.
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`

## `scripts/fp/traffic/junctions.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Junction control (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §2): 4-way traffic lights on cross tiles (N-S green, amber, all-red, E-W green, ...), priority to the through road on tees, pedestrian walk phases, and the street furniture that shows them: light poles at the four corners, pedestrian signals at both ends of every zebra, and stop or yield signs on tee stems. Lamp states are per-instance material_override swaps from shared on/off materials, never edits of a material.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/mesh_kit.gd")`
- `GREEN = 0`
- `AMBER = 1`
- `RED = 2`
- `T_GREEN = 12.0`: Phase lengths, real seconds at 1x (multiplied out by sim.speed through the clock).
- `T_AMBER = 3.0`
- `T_ALLRED = 1.0`
- `CYCLE = 2.0 * (T_GREEN + T_AMBER + T_ALLRED)`
- `WALK_START = 4.5`: People start across a signalled zebra only this early in its walk phase, so they clear the carriageway before the cross traffic gets green.
- `POLE_AT = 0.42`: Corner poles at (±0.42, ±0.42); masts along local -X reach over the inbound lane.
- `MAST = 5.5 * WS.M`
- `PED_SIGNAL_AT = WS.ZEBRA_FAR + 0.3 * WS.M`: Pedestrian signals stand in the curb furniture band just beyond the far edge of their zebra (away from the junction), beside the crossing rather than in its path.
- `CORNERS = [Vector2(1, -1), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(-1, 1), Vector2(-1, -1)]`: Corners 0..3 = NE, SE, SW, NW: offsets and the approach arm each pole's heads face.
- `CORNER_ARM = [2, 3, 0, 1]`: NE serves northbound traffic (from the S arm), SE eastbound (W arm), SW southbound (N arm), NW westbound (E arm): each on the far side of the junction, mast over the lane.
- `LAMP_COLS = [Color(1.0, 0.12, 0.06), Color(1.0, 0.55, 0.05), Color(0.1, 1.0, 0.45)]`
- `POLE_COL = Color(0.22, 0.23, 0.24)`
- `HOUSING_COL = Color(0.06, 0.065, 0.07)`
- `CONCRETE = Color(0.55, 0.54, 0.52)`
- `SIGN_RED = Color(0.62, 0.04, 0.05)`
- `SIGN_WHITE = Color(0.92, 0.92, 0.9)`

### Properties

- `props: Dictionary`: tile -> {"node": Node3D, "groups": Array[MeshInstance3D] (axis * 3 + colour), "peds": Array[GeometryInstance3D] per (axis * 2 + walk), "poles": Array[Node3D], "state": int}

### Functions

- `func setup(p_lg: LG, p_root: Node3D) -> void`
- `func offset(i: int) -> float`
- `func phase(i: int) -> Array`: [axis green (0 N-S, 1 E-W), state GREEN/AMBER/RED for that axis, seconds into the state].
- `func light(i: int, e: int) -> int`: Signal for traffic entering cross tile i from arm e (GREEN when the tile has no lights).
- `func green_left(i: int, e: int) -> float`: Seconds of green left for arm e (0 when not green).
- `func ped_walk(i: int, arm: int) -> bool`: True when people may step onto the zebra across arm `arm` of signalled tile i: its walk phase follows the parallel green (zebras across N/S arms walk with E-W green).
- `func ped_lamp(i: int, arm: int) -> bool`: True while the walk lamp of that zebra shows "walk" (the whole parallel green).
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`: (Re)builds the furniture of every junction tile.
- `func build_props(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds the furniture of tile i (none unless it is a tee or a cross).
- `func light_pole(i: int, corner: int) -> Node3D`: The light pole on cross tile i at corner (0..3 = NE, SE, SW, NW), or null.
- `func update_lamps(p: Vector3, r: float) -> void`: Lamp states of cross tiles near p (within r): swaps materials only on change.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Right-hand lane graph over the road tiles (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §1). Pure data: every lane is a polyline sampled every STEP units with cumulative lengths, keyed by (tile, entry edge, exit edge) so a rebuild keeps lane identity (agents hold Lane references). Geometry mirrors RoadTopology and the road GLBs: lane centres LANE_OFFSET right of travel (PASS_OFFSET beside parked cars), corner arcs about the shared tile corner, junction moves from the stop line to the exit edge, a U-turn loop on ends. Also owns the curb parking slots and the blocked-tile set.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `HEAP = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/heap.gd")`
- `STEP = 0.02`
- `DIRS = [Vector2(0, -1), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(-1, 0)]`: Arm directions in N, E, S, W order (RoadTopology bit order); y is world +Z.
- `OPP = [2, 3, 0, 1]`
- `STRAIGHT = 0`: Lane kinds.
- `CORNER = 1`
- `APPROACH = 2`
- `MOVE = 3`
- `UTURN = 4`
- `STOP_FRONT = WS.STOP_LINE + WS.STOP_BAR`: Car fronts stop here, measured from the junction centre: on the approach edge of the painted stop line (WS.STOP_LINE, roads.py), which lies just outside the zebra.
- `MOVE_FROM = 0.35`: Where approaches hand over to junction movements. It predates the stop line's move outward and stays put so the movement curves (and their timing) are unchanged; the hold is at STOP_FRONT.
- `ZEBRA_MID = (WS.ZEBRA_NEAR + WS.ZEBRA_FAR) * 0.5`
- `SLOT_ALONG = 3.0 * WS.M`: Curb parking: two slots per side of a straight tile, centres 3 m either side of the middle (6 m spacing); slot k: side k / 2 (0 = right of the run direction), along -/+ for k % 2.
- `SLOTS = 4`
- `SHIFT_LEN = 0.2`: Length of the lateral shift between LANE_OFFSET and PASS_OFFSET at a tile end.
- `SLOT_EDGE_CLEAR = SHIFT_LEN + 0.31 + 0.14`: A slot is unusable when a fixed-offset edge (no compatible straight beyond it) is closer than this along the run: the shift zone plus half the longest moving vehicle (bus) plus half the longest parked one, so no moving AABB ever overlaps a parked AABB.
- `A_LAT = 2.2 * WS.M`: Lateral acceleration used for curve speed limits (2.2 m/s²).
- `UTURN_R = 0.235`: Loop radius of the cul-de-sac U-turn about the turning circle centre.
- `CONFLICT_DIST = 0.11`: Two move lanes whose centrelines come closer than this conflict (a car is 2.1 m wide).
- `BLOCKED_COST = 12.0`: Route cost factor through a blocked tile for the vehicles that may cross one.

### Properties

- `lanes: Array`: id -> Lane or null
- `tiles: Dictionary`: tile -> TileInfo
- `blocked: Dictionary`: tile -> true (broken road, crash or downed line)
- `slots: Dictionary`: Occupied curb slots: (tile * SLOTS + k) -> owner key (String).
- `parked_sides: Dictionary`: Occupied slots per side: (tile * 2 + side) -> count.
- `stop_sides: Dictionary`: Bus-stop sides: tile -> side index whose curb is kept free for the bus.
- `builds: int`: tile rebuilds since setup (tests)
- `bulk: bool`: While true, slot changes skip the lane rebuild (the caller rebuilds once afterwards).
- `dirty: Dictionary`: Tiles whose lanes were rebuilt since the last take_dirty() (agents re-place their nodes).

### Inner classes

- `Lane`: One lane: a directed polyline on one road tile.
- `TileInfo`: Per road tile: its mask, piece and lanes.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim) -> void`
- `func clear() -> void`
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`: Rebuilds every road tile in sim.active.
- `func rebuild_around(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds tile i and its four neighbours (a road tile was built or cleared).
- `func neighbours(i: int) -> Array[int]`: In-bounds 4-neighbour tile indices of i.
- `func is_empty() -> bool`
- `func lane_count() -> int`
- `func info(i: int) -> TileInfo`
- `func across(i: int, e: int) -> int`: Tile across edge e of tile i, or -1.
- `func entry(i: int, e: int) -> Array`: Lanes that begin at edge e of tile i (a junction's approach, else the through lane).
- `func next_lanes(l: Lane) -> Array`: Lanes an agent can take after reaching the end of l.
- `func prev_lanes(l: Lane) -> Array`: Lanes that end where l begins (upstream), for gap checks.
- `func lane_between(i: int, fe: int, te: int) -> Lane`: The lane on tile i from entry edge fe to exit edge te (a move for junctions), or null.
- `func pos_at(l: Lane, s: float) -> Vector2`: World xz of the point at distance s along l (clamped to the lane).
- `func tan_at(l: Lane, s: float) -> Vector2`: Unit tangent of l at distance s.
- `func project(l: Lane, p: Vector2) -> float`: Distance along l of the point closest to p (xz).
- `func pass_factor(l: Lane, s: float) -> float`: How far a straight lane is pulled in toward PASS_OFFSET at s (0 = LANE_OFFSET, 1 = PASS_OFFSET).
- `func refresh_blocked() -> bool`: Re-reads broken roads and road-blocking events (car_crash, power_line). Returns true on change.
- `func is_blocked(i: int) -> bool`
- `func parkable(i: int) -> bool`: True when straight tile i can take curb parking at all (not a bridge, not a junction).
- `func run_dir(i: int) -> Vector2`: Run direction (xz) of straight tile i.
- `func side_of_heading(i: int, h: Vector2) -> int`: Side index (0 right of run_dir, 1 left) of straight tile i that a vehicle heading h drives on.
- `func slot_pose(i: int, k: int) -> Array`: [pos: Vector2 (world xz), heading: Vector2] of curb slot k of straight tile i. The car faces the traffic on its side (right-hand).
- `func slot_valid(i: int, k: int) -> bool`: True when slot k of tile i is usable: a parkable straight, clear of fixed-offset edges (where the moving lane cannot shift outside the tile) and of a bus-stop curb.
- `func slot_free(i: int, k: int) -> bool`
- `func slot_owner(i: int, k: int) -> String`
- `func set_slot(i: int, k: int, owner: String) -> void`: Marks curb slot k of tile i as taken by owner (or freed with ""), rebuilding the lanes beside it when its side changes between empty and occupied.
- `func side_parked(i: int, sidx: int) -> bool`
- `func slots_on_heading(i: int, h: Vector2) -> Array[int]`: Slot indices on the curb a vehicle heading h on straight tile i would pull into.
- `func rebuild_tile(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds the lanes of tile i from sim.kind and RoadTopology (removes them when it is no road).
- `func take_dirty() -> Dictionary`: Tiles rebuilt since the last call (and clears the set).
- `static func entry_pt(e: int, off: float) -> Vector2`: Tile-local entry point on edge e for traffic heading into the tile at lateral offset off.
- `static func exit_pt(e: int, off: float) -> Vector2`: Tile-local exit point on edge e for traffic leaving the tile at lateral offset off.
- `func lanes_along(seq: Array[int], fe0: int = -1, te_last: int = -1) -> Array`: Lane path along a sequence of road tiles: for each tile the lane from the edge it is entered by to the edge toward the next tile, with junction approaches before their moves. fe0 is the entry edge of the first tile (-1: any), te_last the exit edge of the last (-1: any). O(tiles). Returns [] when a step has no lane.
- `func edge_between(a: int, b: int) -> int`: Edge of tile a that faces adjacent tile b, or -1.
- `func lanes_through(i: int, fe: int, te: int) -> Array`: Lanes crossing tile i entering at fe and leaving at te (either may be -1 for "any").
- `func astar(from: Lane, goals: Dictionary, max_nodes: int = 3000, through_blocked: bool = false) -> Array`: A* over lanes from the end of `from` to the end of any lane in `goals` (lane id -> true), costing length / limit * (1 + 2 * traffic) and avoiding blocked tiles (through_blocked: crews and bus lines may cross them, at BLOCKED_COST times the cost, when there is no way round). At most max_nodes expansions. Returns the lanes after `from` up to and including the goal lane, or [].

## `scripts/fp/traffic/mesh_kit.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Builds merged, vertex-coloured meshes for E's procedural stand-ins (traffic lights, signs, the far LOD of every vehicle and person model). One surface per mesh, so a whole junction's poles or a whole car costs one draw.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`

### Properties

- `lamp_alpha: float`: Vertex alpha for surfaces whose material emits (lamps); 1.0 leaves every vertex opaque-flagged.

### Functions

- `func begin() -> void`
- `func box(xf: Transform3D, sz: Vector3, c: Color) -> void`: Axis-aligned box of size sz (units) centred at the origin of xf, coloured c.
- `func cyl(xf: Transform3D, r0: float, r1: float, h: float, c: Color, sides: int = 10, caps: bool = true) -> void`: Cylinder along +Y from the origin of xf: radius r0 at the bottom, r1 at the top, height h.
- `func disc(xf: Transform3D, r: float, c: Color, sides: int = 12, rot: float = 0.0) -> void`: Flat regular polygon (disc with `sides` corners) of radius r in the xf's XY plane, facing +Z.
- `func tri_plate(xf: Transform3D, a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c3: Vector3, c: Color) -> void`: Flat triangle facing +Z in xf's XY plane.
- `func mesh(xf: Transform3D, m: Mesh, overrides: Array = []) -> void`: Appends every surface of a mesh, coloured by its material albedo (emission adds a glow tint).
- `func node(root: Node3D) -> void`: Merges every MeshInstance3D under root (in root space) into one vertex-coloured mesh.
- `func commit() -> ArrayMesh`: The merged mesh (null when nothing was added).
- `static func vc_material(rough: float = 0.6, metal: float = 0.0) -> StandardMaterial3D`: Shared opaque material for vertex-coloured meshes.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/occupants.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Drivers seated in the moving vehicles nearest the camera. Only while a vehicle draws its full model: those have see-through glass, a cabin and a Seat_Driver marker at the driver's hip point (tools/blender/realcity/vehicles2.py); the merged far LODs have opaque glass. A driver is the car's resident (people.dress picks the same avatar and stature the resident walks with) or an ambient body from the city seed, posed once in the sit loop with its mixers off, so a seated body costs its draws and nothing per frame beyond its transform.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `PPL = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd")`
- `CAP = 12`
- `RANGE = 30.0 * WS.M`
- `SEAT_NODE = "Seat_Driver"`
- `SIT = &"sit"`: The sit loop is held at this time (s): hands on the lap, head level.
- `SIT_AT = 1.0`
- `PROXY_ID = 1 << 24`: Walker ids seed ambient dressing; drivers use their own range so they do not copy a walker.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_people: PPL) -> void`
- `func sync(cars: Array, cam: Vector3, residents: Variant) -> void`: Seats a driver in each of the CAP nearest moving vehicles within RANGE that show their full model, and releases the rest. Call between people.begin and people.finish.
- `func clear() -> void`: Releases every seated body.
- `func body_of(id: int) -> PPL.Body`: The seated body in car id (null when it has no driver drawn).
- `func seat_point(node: Node3D) -> Variant`: The seat marker's position in the full model's space, cached on the node (null without one).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/people.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Animated people from HC's roster (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md deliverable 9, TPS_PLAN §1.10-1.11). Rocketbox bodies on Godot's humanoid skeleton, picked by job, gender and crc32(resident id) for residents and by HC's ambient weights for the crowd, each under a CharacterRoot scaled to a jittered stature, animated by the gender's shared library plus three clips layered here at load (walk_carry and carry_idle hold a box, walk_phone a phone at the ear), with the playback rate matched to the walking speed so feet do not slide. LOD tiers by camera distance, 10 % hysteresis: T0  <= 12 m, max 8   AnimationTree (state machine, 0.25 s crossfades), every frame, shadows T1  12-30 m           AnimationPlayer advanced by hand, 30 Hz to 20 m (shadows) else 15 Hz T2  30-60 m           the same at 10 Hz, no shadows T3  to VIS_PERSON     HC's static mid-stride <Name>_lod1 in one MultiMesh per avatar T1 and T2 share a cap of SKIN_CAP bodies on screen, and everything stays inside DRAW_CAP character draws. Off-screen bodies keep their pose with their mixer inactive (and go back to the pool after OFF_KEEP). Bodies are pooled per avatar and instanced at most NEW_PER_FRAME per frame. Body and lod1 scenes load on background threads when first needed (a first load takes 25-150 ms; loading every avatar up front costs ~100 MB of textures); a walker whose body is still loading waits at T3, undrawn while its lod1 loads too. Asset building lives in people_kit.gd.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd")`
- `T0_R = 12.0 * WS.M`
- `T0_CAP = 8`
- `T1_R = 30.0 * WS.M`
- `T1_NEAR = 20.0 * WS.M`
- `T2_R = 60.0 * WS.M`
- `HYST = 1.1`
- `SKIN_CAP = 40`
- `DRAW_CAP = 150`
- `HZ_NEAR = 30.0`
- `HZ_MID = 15.0`
- `HZ_FAR = 10.0`
- `NEW_PER_FRAME = 4`
- `OFF_KEEP = 4.0`
- `LOOK_CAP = 6`
- `XFADE = 0.25`
- `WALK_ON = 0.35 * WS.M`: A person counts as walking above WALK_ON and as standing below WALK_OFF (u/s, as drawn).
- `WALK_OFF = 0.2 * WS.M`
- `RATE_MIN = 0.5`
- `RATE_MAX = 1.6`
- `PERSON_FADE = 0.4`: People fade out over this last stretch before VIS_PERSON (T3).
- `CULL_UP = 0.9 * WS.M`: Frustum test: a sphere around the body (metres above the feet, radius).
- `CULL_R = 1.3 * WS.M`
- `STATES = [ &"idle", &"idle_look", &"idle_wait", &"walk", &"walk_carry", &"walk_phone", &"carry_i...`
- `LOCO = [&"walk", &"walk_carry", &"walk_phone"]`
- `STILL = [&"", &"carry_idle", &"phone"]`
- `BOX_COLOR = Color(0.62, 0.47, 0.3)`

### Properties

- `blocking: bool`: Load body and lod1 scenes on the calling thread (deterministic tests), not in the background.

### Inner classes

- `Avatar`: One roster body (never a hero).
- `Body`: One instanced body: CharacterRoot > the body scene (Armature/GeneralSkeleton/Body, Anim, Tree).

### Functions

- `func load_assets() -> bool`: Loads the roster and both libraries and builds the layered clips and the T0 tree. False (with `why`) when HC's characters are missing: E then draws the legacy static people.
- `func reset(p_root: Node3D, city_seed: int) -> void`: Starts drawing under p_root (a new world): frees every body, keeps the loaded assets.
- `func clear() -> void`: Frees every body and LOD layer.
- `func crc32(s: String) -> int`: CRC-32 (IEEE, as zlib) of s's UTF-8 bytes.
- `func resident_gender(rid: String, full_name: String) -> String`: Gender of a resident: HC's name_gender for the first name, else crc32(id) & 1 (1 = f).
- `func resident_avatar(rid: String, full_name: String, job: String) -> int`: Avatar index for a resident: the job's pool for the gender, else the gender's casual pool, indexed by crc32(id). -1 when nothing fits.
- `func stature(g: String, u: float) -> float`: Stature (m) for a gender and a 0..1 jitter value.
- `func dress(w: WK.Walker, residents: Variant) -> void`: Gives w its avatar and stature (once): residents by their id, ambient walkers from the city seed.
- `func avatar_name(w: WK.Walker) -> String`: Avatar name of walker w ("" before it is dressed).
- `func scale_of(w: WK.Walker) -> float`: CharacterRoot scale of w: WS.M * h_target / rest_height_m.
- `func authored_speed(w: WK.Walker, clip: StringName) -> float`: Ground speed (u/s) clip covers at playback rate 1 on w's body.
- `func head_of(w: WK.Walker, base: Vector3) -> Vector3`: World position of w's Head bone while a body draws it, else an estimate from its stature.
- `func begin(delta: float, adt: float, cam: Camera3D, cam_pos: Vector3, look_at: Vector3) -> void`: Starts a frame: delta is real seconds, adt game seconds (delta * sim.speed).
- `func on_screen(p: Vector3) -> bool`: True when a body at feet position p could be on screen.
- `func add(w: WK.Walker, d: float, residents: Variant) -> void`: Queues walker w (eased already, d = camera distance) and advances its clip.
- `func finish() -> void`: Assigns tiers, attaches, advances and releases bodies, and fills the T3 layers.
- `func seat(w: WK.Walker) -> bool`: Gives dressed walker w a body outside the tiers (a seated driver, posed by occupants.gd); false while none is free. release(w) hands it back.
- `func release(w: WK.Walker) -> void`: A walker leaves for good (removed): its body goes back to the pool.
- `func finish_loads() -> void`: Waits for every background scene load still running and keeps the results.
- `func stats() -> Dictionary`: anim_stats() for G2's bench: tier counts on screen, microseconds advancing mixers this frame, character draws (skinned surfaces and boxes on screen plus two per T3 avatar layer).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Asset building for people.gd: the layered clips (a box held in both hands, a phone at the ear), the shared T0 AnimationTree, and HC's lod1 meshes as dither-fading T3 MultiMesh layers.

### Constants

- `ARM_PARTS = [ "Shoulder", "UpperArm", "LowerArm", "Hand", "ThumbMetacarpal", "ThumbProximal", "Thum...`: Layered clips: the arm bones taken from another clip's pose at a fixed time.
- `CARRY_AT = 0.0`
- `PHONE_AT = 0.5`
- `NEEDS = [ &"idle", &"walk", &"talk", &"talk_2", &"phone", &"carry", &"idle_look", &"idle_wait",...`
- `T3_SHADER = """`

### Functions

- `static func layered_library(hc: AnimationLibrary) -> Variant`: A copy of HC's library with walk_carry, carry_idle and walk_phone added; the name of the first missing clip in NEEDS instead when it lacks one.
- `static func layer(base: Animation, over: Animation, bones: Array[String], at: float, nm: String) -> Animation`: base with the rotations of `bones` replaced by over's pose at time `at` (constant keys).
- `static func build_tree(states: Array[StringName], xfade: float) -> AnimationNodeBlendTree`: The T0 tree, shared by every body: state machine (every state reaches every other with a crossfade) -> TimeSeek (handovers from T1) -> TimeScale (playback rate) -> output.
- `static func t3_shader() -> Shader`
- `static func lod_mesh(ps: PackedScene, shader: Shader) -> Array`: The first mesh of a lod1 scene as [ArrayMesh with the fade shader, its transform in the scene]; [] when the scene has no mesh.
- `static func t3_layer(nm: String, mesh: Mesh) -> MultiMeshInstance3D`: An empty, hidden T3 layer for mesh (custom data carries the fade).
- `static func fill(mmi: MultiMeshInstance3D, xfs: Array[Transform3D], cols: Array[Color]) -> void`: Shows xfs (fade in the alpha of cols) on mmi, growing its buffer by doubling.
- `static func crc32(s: String) -> int`: CRC-32 (IEEE, as zlib) of s's UTF-8 bytes.
- `static func pose(sk: Skeleton3D, bone: int) -> Transform3D`: Bone pose in skeleton space from the local poses.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/render.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Draws E's agents (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §3 Draw calls). Vehicles: the full GLB only within NEAR of the camera (pooled per model, capped), beyond that one MultiMeshInstance3D per model built from a single-surface, vertex-coloured merge of the GLB (H's <name>_lod1.glb when it exists), with shadows to SHADOW_DIST and none beyond. Parked cars go through a static layer rebuilt only when the parked set changes or the camera moves. Brake lights, siren flashes and wheel spin on full models; after dark their head and tail lamps light up, the nearest moving vehicles throw headlight beams, and the head and tail lamps of the merged ones glow. Responding crews near the camera wash their surroundings in flashing siren light. People (the legacy static bodies, until HC's rigged ones): every distance draws the merged body through the people shader, which swings the legs and arms from per-instance stride data and dithers people in and out (spawned in view, or at the edge of VIS_PERSON). Same geometry and colours as the GLB, one draw per body model and layer.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/mesh_kit.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `NEAR = 2.0`
- `NEAR_OUT = 2.25`
- `SHADOW_DIST = 3.0`
- `CAP_VEHICLES = 40`: Full-detail caps until H's lod1 files and HC's tiers land (contract: 40).
- `CAP_PEOPLE = 40`
- `MAX_INSTANCE_PER_FRAME = 4`
- `SIREN_COLS = {"firetruck": [Color(1.0, 0.12, 0.08), Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.15)], "ambulance": [Color(1.0,...`
- `L_MID = 0`: MultiMesh layers per model: moving mid (shadows), moving far, static mid (shadows), static far.
- `L_FAR = 1`
- `L_SMID = 2`
- `L_SFAR = 3`
- `LEG_SWING = 0.38`: Stride swing of the people shader, radians at full stride (legs; arms swing opposite).
- `ARM_SWING = 0.3`
- `PERSON_FADE = 0.4`: People fade out over this last stretch before VIS_PERSON.
- `LAMP_ALPHA = 0.5`: Merged meshes flag lamp vertices (emissive source materials) with this vertex alpha.
- `LAMPS_ON = 0.35`: Lamps count as on above this darkness (sky night 0..1).
- `BEAMS = 8`: Headlight beams after dark: spot lights on the moving vehicles nearest the camera (no shadows).
- `BEAM_DIST = 4.0`
- `BEAM_RANGE = 34.0 * WS.M`
- `BEAM_ANGLE = 30.0`
- `BEAM_ENERGY = 2.4`
- `BEAM_DECAY = 0.5`: Distance falloff exponent of a beam: gentler than inverse distance, so someone standing in front of a waiting car is lit, not blown out, while the road 10-30 m ahead still gets a pool.
- `BEAM_HEIGHT = 0.65 * WS.M`
- `WASHES = 3`: Siren light washes: flashing omni lights on responding crews near the camera.
- `WASH_DIST = 3.0`
- `WASH_RANGE = 14.0 * WS.M`
- `PEOPLE_SHADER = """`
- `VEHICLE_SHADER = """`

### Inner classes

- `Model`: One drawable model.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_root: Node3D) -> void`
- `func model_for(path: String, scale: float, person: bool = false) -> int`: Index of the model for a GLB path (loaded once), or -1 when it cannot load.
- `func model_proc(key: String, mesh: Mesh, size: Vector3) -> int`: A procedural model (one vertex-coloured mesh, drawn through the MultiMesh layers only).
- `func model(i: int) -> Model`
- `func begin(dt: float) -> void`: Starts a frame of moving agents (the static layer keeps its lists).
- `func set_glow(g: float) -> void`: Lamp glow of the merged vehicles (0 by day, 1 at night).
- `func begin_static() -> void`: Starts a rebuild of the static (parked) layer.
- `func draw_car(c: VH.Car, xf: Transform3D, d: float, vis_end: float, brake: bool, siren: String, spin: float) -> void`
- `func draw_parked(c: VH.Car, xf: Transform3D, d: float, vis_end: float) -> void`: A parked car into the static layer (between begin_static and finish_static).
- `func draw_walker(w: WK.Walker, xf: Transform3D, d: float, vis_end: float, phase: float = 0.0) -> void`: A person: always the merged body through the people shader (stride and opacity per instance).
- `func release_car(c: VH.Car) -> void`: Returns a vehicle's full node to its pool.
- `func release_walker(w: WK.Walker) -> void`
- `func finish() -> void`: Writes the moving MultiMesh layers for this frame, and aims the headlight beams and siren washes at the nearest candidates.
- `func finish_static() -> void`: Writes the static (parked) layers.
- `func clear() -> void`: Frees every pooled and live node.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Pedestrian network (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §3 Pedestrians): sidewalk polylines whose centrelines sit at the middle of WS.PED_BAND from the road centreline, joined around junction corners, around corner tiles and around cul-de-sacs, plus a zebra edge across every arm of a tee or cross. Nodes are merged by position, so tiles join at their shared edges.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `HEAP = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/heap.gd")`
- `LAT = (WS.PED_BAND[0] + WS.PED_BAND[1]) * 0.5`: Walking line: the middle of the pedestrian band.
- `ZEBRA = LG.ZEBRA_MID`
- `STEP = 0.04`
- `END_R = WS.END_CIRCLE_R + (LAT - WS.ROAD_HALF)`: Loop radius around a cul-de-sac's turning circle (its centre is offset toward the closed end).
- `DIRS = LG.DIRS`

### Properties

- `adj: Array`: node id -> Array[int] edge ids
- `edges: Array`: id -> PedEdge or null
- `by_tile: Dictionary`: tile -> Array[PedEdge]
- `zebras: Dictionary`: (tile * 4 + arm) -> zebra PedEdge.

### Inner classes

- `PedEdge`: One walkable edge between two nodes.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim) -> void`
- `func clear() -> void`
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`
- `func rebuild_around(i: int) -> void`
- `func edge_count() -> int`
- `func edge(id: int) -> PedEdge`
- `func zebra_at(tile: int, arm: int) -> PedEdge`
- `func pos_at(e: PedEdge, t: float) -> Vector3`: Point and height at distance t along e.
- `func dir_at(e: PedEdge, t: float) -> Vector2`: Unit direction of e at t (a -> b).
- `func other(e: PedEdge, n: int) -> int`: The node at the far end of edge e from node n.
- `func nearest_node(p: Vector2, i: int) -> int`: Nearest node to world xz point p among the nodes of tile i (and its edges), or -1.
- `func nearest_on_tile(p: Vector2, i: int) -> Array`: Nearest point on a sidewalk (non-zebra) edge of tile i to p: [edge, t] or [].
- `func route(from: int, to: int, max_nodes: int = 6000) -> Array`: A* over the network from node `from` to node `to`: [[edge id, dir (+1 a->b, -1 b->a)], ...] or [] when unreachable within max_nodes expansions.
- `func rebuild_tile(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds the sidewalk edges of tile i (removes them when it is no longer a road).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/traffic_feature.gd`

extends `FpFeature`

Traffic and pedestrians on lanes (slice E, docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md): one road-agent system for first person. A right-hand lane graph with traffic lights and tee priority, IDM car following, residents' own trips played out from their minds' plans (trip_started), ambient commuters and pedestrians around the player, curb parking, buses on seeded lines, trucks and emergency crews (CityLife.external), and the ResidentAvatars hooks (ResidentAvatars.external). Everyone stops for the player. Motion runs on delta * sim.speed, so pause freezes it.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `JN = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/junctions.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `RD = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/render.gd")`
- `AMB = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/ambient.gd")`
- `TRIPS = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/trips.gd")`
- `FLEETS = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/fleets.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/mesh_kit.gd")`
- `PPL = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people.gd")`
- `CS = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/contact_shadows.gd")`
- `OCC = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/occupants.gd")`
- `MAX_STEP = 1.0 / 30.0`
- `CAR_PREFIXES = ["sedan", "hatch", "suv", "taxi", "van", "pickup", "coupe"]`
- `TELEPORT = 2.0`: A jump of the player beyond this in one frame is a teleport: the street is refilled around them.
- `WARM_SECONDS = 14.0`
- `PICK_PX = 26.0`
- `PHOTO_BACK = 1.3`: The traffic photo stands this far from the junction centre along the arm.
- `LINE_RETRY = 10.0`: Seconds between attempts to rebuild bus lines that no longer match the roads.
- `CLAIM_SPEED = 0.5 * WS.M`: The player can take a parked car, their own, or an ambient car stopped below this speed.

### Properties

- `people: PPL`: HC's animated people (deliverable 9); ok == false draws the legacy static people instead.
- `jitter_enabled: bool`: Test hooks: departure jitter on or off; auto_step false keeps _process from advancing time.
- `ambient_enabled: bool`: Test hook: false stops the ambient filler (no spawns, no removals).

### Functions

- `func feature_id() -> String`
- `func setup(p_ctx: FpContext) -> void`
- `func teardown() -> void`
- `func on_world_rebuilt() -> void`
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`: Advances everything by dt seconds of game-scaled time (test hook; _process calls it in steps of at most 1/30 s).
- `func sync_visuals(delta: float) -> void`: Draws every agent (full models near, MultiMesh LOD far) and updates lamp states. Parked cars are redrawn only when the parked set changes or the camera moves a little.
- `func on_screen(p: Vector3) -> bool`: True when p could be on screen now (inside the camera frustum and within car range).
- `func is_far(p: Vector3) -> bool`: True when p is beyond the traffic radius of the player.
- `func player_dist(p: Vector2) -> float`
- `func vehicle_model(kind: String) -> int`: Model of a fleet vehicle kind (bus, truck, garbage_truck, firetruck, ambulance, police).
- `func car_model_for(rid: String) -> int`: A resident's own car model: the same pick as ResidentAvatars (hash of the id over the list).
- `func person_model_for(rid: String) -> int`
- `func dims(m: int) -> Vector3`: World size (x width, y height, z length) of a model.
- `func bike_model() -> int`: A cyclist: H's bicycle when present, else a procedural bicycle and rider (one mesh).
- `func door_point(lot: int) -> Vector3`: Where a person enters or leaves lot i: H's Door_<n> empty when the building has one, else the middle of its front edge (facing its frontage road).
- `func place_label(lot: int) -> String`
- `func street_label(tile: int) -> String`
- `func outdoor_spot(lot: int, rid: String) -> Array`: Where a resident stands outdoors at lot: [pos, yaw] in a small group (they face its middle).
- `func spawn_spot_near(start: Vector2i, length: float) -> Array`: A spot for a fleet vehicle at tile `start` (or anywhere fitting the spawn rules): [lane, s] or [].
- `func free_worker(job: String) -> String`: A resident with `job` who is at work, not on a trip and not already driving a fleet vehicle.
- `func bus_choice(seq: Array[int], dest: int) -> Array`
- `func bus_at(bus: VH.Car, line: int, tile: int) -> void`
- `func stop_point(i: int) -> Vector3`: Where people wait at the bus stop on tile i: on the walking band in front of the shelter.
- `func spawn_fleet(kind: String, start: Vector2i) -> void`: Adds one vehicle of a fleet (bus, truck, garbage_truck) when its own rules allow.
- `func dispatch_crew(kind: String, station: Vector2i, target: Vector2i) -> void`: Sends an emergency crew of `kind` from road tile station to road tile target.
- `func fleet_size(kind: String) -> int`: Current size of a fleet (CityLife's census compares it with its target).
- `func vehicle_counts() -> Dictionary`: {buses, trucks, crews, boats, aircraft}: road fleets from E, boats and aircraft from CityLife.
- `func on_resident_moved(r: Dictionary) -> void`: Residents.resident_moved, forwarded (state only: trips spawn from trip_started).
- `func position_of(id: String) -> Vector3`: Live position of a resident while drawn; else the tile they are at.
- `func avatar_pick(screen_pos: Vector2, cam: Camera3D) -> String`: The drawn resident closest to screen_pos within 26 px of camera cam, or "".
- `func avatar_counts() -> Dictionary`: {walking, driving, standing, total} for the HUD and the smoke prints.
- `func agents_near(p: Vector3, r: float) -> Array`: Agents near p for the minimap and audio (moving vehicles and people on foot; parked cars are left out): [{id, pos, vel, speed, kind, driver_id, heading, stalled_s}]. heading follows S0 §11 (forward = (-sin h, 0, -cos h)), so it holds for stopped agents too; vel is u/s. The entries are each agent's own dictionary, refreshed once per frame: read them now, copy one to keep it.
- `func agents_packed(p: Vector3, r: float) -> Dictionary`: The cheap form of agents_near for per-frame consumers: parallel packed arrays {"pos": PackedVector3Array, "vel": PackedVector3Array, "heading": PackedFloat32Array, "kind": PackedStringArray} of the agents within r of p (same conventions, no dictionaries).
- `func visible_near(p: Vector3, r: float) -> Array`: Visible named residents near p (on foot, in a vehicle, or standing outdoors; never indoors).
- `func is_resident_visible(id: String) -> bool`
- `func pick(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, max_dist: float) -> Dictionary`: Interaction pick (S0 §10): residents on foot, ambient pedestrians, vehicles (parked included).
- `func blockers_near(p: Vector3, r: float) -> Array`: Optional, for A: world AABBs of stopped vehicles near p (parked cars included). While the player drives, moving vehicles block too, and the player's own car does not.
- `func enter_target(p: Vector3, r: float) -> Dictionary`: The car the player could get into from p: the nearest one they may take whose body is within r of p, as {"id", "label", "pos", "dist"}; {} when none (or while they drive).
- `func claim_car(id: int) -> Dictionary`: Hands car id to the player: an ambient, decor or resident car is swapped for a player car of the same model where it stands (its owner's trip carries on without it). Returns the car's {"id", "pos", "yaw", "length", "half_w", "height"}, or {} when it cannot be taken.
- `func drive_car(pos: Vector3, yaw: float, v: float, a: float) -> void`: Poses the driven car (speed v signed, acceleration a) and its model at once, so the car and the seated hero move in the same frame.
- `func leave_car() -> void`: The player gets out: the car stays where it stands until it is far away and out of sight.
- `func driven_id() -> int`: Id of the car the player drives, -1 on foot.
- `func seat_offset() -> Variant`: The driver's hip point in the driven car's own frame (+Z forward), or null until its full model is drawn (the merged far LOD has no seat).
- `func light_pole(i: int, corner: int) -> Node3D`: The traffic-light pole on cross tile i at corner (0..3 = NE, SE, SW, NW), or null.
- `func anchor_of(id: String) -> Vector3`: Live head anchor of resident id while drawn (else above where they are). With HC bodies it is the Head bone's world position (an estimate from the stature while no body draws them).
- `func anim_stats() -> Dictionary`: Animated-people stats for G2's bench: {"t0", "t1", "t2", "t3"} people on screen per LOD tier, "anim_us" microseconds advancing mixers this frame (T0 trees included), "char_draws" character draws (shadows extra), plus "off" (off-screen bodies holding their pose), "bodies" (instanced) and "people_us" (the whole people pass). Legacy static people report their shader draws only.
- `func resident_avatar(id: String) -> String`: The HC avatar a resident is drawn with ("" without HC bodies): job pool by gender, crc32(id).
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`
- `func self_test() -> Dictionary`
- `func photo_shots() -> Array`: The "traffic" shot: the most built-up cross tile with lights, seen at eye height from the sidewalk of one of its arms, 1.3 tiles back, beside the inbound lane: the queue at the light, the zebra in front of it, the poles and the cross traffic.
- `func photo_prepare() -> void`: Photo tour hook: refill the street around the next shot (the tour holds sim speed 0) and time the warm-up so it ends with the shot's approach on red and the cross street green, 5 s in: the queue has formed and people are on the zebra in front of it.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/trips.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Resident trips (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §4): the AI link. Residents.trip_started arrives when a mind's plan sends someone somewhere; the sim counts them there at once, and this plays the trip out at real speed behind it. car: walk from the door to their own parked car, drive the sim's route lane by lane, pull into a curb slot at the destination, walk to the door. walk: sidewalks and zebras door to door. bus: walk to a stop on the route, wait for a line that serves the destination, ride, walk. bike: a cyclist at the carriageway edge. Residents outdoors at their destination stand there in small groups. Beyond the traffic radius a trip is data only.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `INSIDE = ["home", "work", "shopping", "working late"]`
- `BUS_WAIT = 90.0`
- `JITTER = 6.0`
- `BIKE_SPEED = 4.0 * WS.M`
- `HEAD = 1.62 * WS.M`
- `SEATED_HEAD = 1.2 * WS.M`

### Properties

- `f: Object`: the traffic feature (helpers: models, doors, visibility)
- `trips: Dictionary`: rid -> Trip
- `cars: Dictionary`: rid -> Car (their own; parked between trips)
- `standing: Dictionary`: rid -> Walker standing outdoors
- `held: Dictionary`: rid -> true while in a conversation

### Inner classes

- `Trip`: One trip in flight.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_f: Object, p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_lg: LG, p_sw: SW, p_vh: VH, p_wk: WK) -> void`
- `func reset() -> void`: Drops every trip, walker and car (a new world); parked positions come back from `parked`.
- `static func inside_state(state: String) -> bool`
- `func jitter(rid: String) -> float`: Departure delay, real seconds at 1x, seeded by (id, day).
- `func on_trip_started(rid: String, from_i: int, to_i: int, mode: String) -> void`
- `func on_moved(r: Dictionary) -> void`: A resident moved without a trip (state only): keeps standing residents in sync.
- `func on_departed(r: Dictionary) -> void`
- `func on_day_started() -> void`: Reconciles parked cars with where their owners now live and work (sim.day_started).
- `func car_of(rid: String, lot: int, toward: int = -1) -> VH.Car`: The resident's own car, creating it (parked near lot, facing road tile `toward` when given) the first time.
- `func walk_plan(a: Vector3, ta: int, b: Vector3, tb: int) -> Array`: Walking plan from world point a (near road tile ta) to b (near tb): a free leg onto the nearest sidewalk, the network (zebras included), and a free leg off it. [] when unreachable.
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`: Per-step trip logic (dt: game-scaled seconds).
- `func on_car_arrived(c: VH.Car) -> void`: A vehicle reached its goal (vehicles.on_arrive).
- `func on_bus_at(bus: VH.Car, line: int, tile: int) -> void`: Bus hooks (fleets): a bus of `line` stands at stop `tile`.
- `func complete_now(tr: Trip) -> void`: Finishes a trip at once: everyone jumps to the destination (a new trip, a load, a lost road).
- `func seed_standing() -> void`: Standing residents for everyone outdoors without a trip (after a rebuild or load).
- `func hold(rid: String, on: bool) -> void`: Conversation: stop the resident's agent and turn it to the player.
- `func walker_of(rid: String) -> WK.Walker`: The walker currently drawing resident rid, or null.
- `func vehicle_of(rid: String) -> VH.Car`: The vehicle resident rid is driving or riding right now, or null.
- `func live_position(rid: String) -> Vector3`: Live position of rid (walker, vehicle), or NAN when not drawn.
- `func anchor(rid: String) -> Vector3`: Head anchor of rid while drawn (speech bubble, conversation two-shot), or NAN.
- `func parked_table() -> Dictionary`: Saved parked table: {rid: [tile, slot]}.
- `func restore_parked(d: Dictionary) -> void`: Restores parked cars from a saved table (only for residents who still exist).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Every road vehicle (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §3): ambient filler, resident cars, buses, trucks, crews and cyclists. Each moving vehicle holds its front's lane and distance s, follows the Intelligent Driver Model behind the next vehicle on its path, a held stop line, a parking or bus-stop goal, people on a zebra it must cross, or the player, and is hard-clamped so it never passes through any of them. Junction entry needs a light, a gap (tees, left turns), a clear box and room on the exit lane. Parked cars stand in curb slots off the lanes. Beyond the traffic radius a vehicle with a destination keeps moving as data only (no lane occupancy, no IDM).

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `IDM = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/idm.gd")`
- `JN = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/junctions.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `SEDAN_HW = 0.063 * WS.VEHICLE_SCALE`: Half width of a sedan at VEHICLE_SCALE (the vehicle PASS_OFFSET is sized for).
- `MIN_GAP = 0.5 * WS.M`: Hard minimum bumper gap; IDM keeps s0 = 2 m, this only stops a car from ever touching.
- `IMPATIENCE = 14.0`: Seconds a held car waits before it stops yielding at all (never at a red light); before that the gap it needs shrinks from the junction's gap to GAP_MIN over GAP_PATIENCE seconds.
- `GAP_MIN = 1.8`
- `GAP_PATIENCE = 8.0`
- `PARK_TIME = 1.6`: Pull-in / pull-out duration at the curb, seconds.
- `BIKE_LAT = WS.ROAD_HALF - 0.04 - WS.LANE_OFFSET`: Cyclists ride this far right of the lane centre (carriageway edge at ROAD_HALF - 0.04).
- `SIREN_RED_SPEED = 5.0 * WS.M`: Through a red light a crew rolls at most this fast.
- `ARRIVE_TOL = 0.45 * WS.M`: A vehicle this close to its goal point, nearly stopped, has arrived (the settle rule stops cars up to 0.3 m short of a held point).
- `BLOCKED_SPEED = 2.5 * WS.M`: Speed past a blocked tile (cars avoid them when choosing a way; committed ones creep by).
- `LOD_FULL = 3.0`: Simulation LOD: within LOD_FULL of the player a vehicle steps every step, out to LOD_NEAR at most every LOD_MID_DT seconds, beyond that every LOD_DT; draws extrapolate in between.
- `LOD_MID_DT = 1.0 / 20.0`
- `LOD_NEAR = 6.0`
- `LOD_DT = 1.0 / 10.0`
- `FAR_SPEED = 0.9`: Data-only vehicles beyond the traffic radius cruise at this share of their own speed.
- `PLAYER = "player"`: Role of the player's own cars: never on a lane, posed by the drive feature or left standing.

### Properties

- `parked_version: int`: Bumped whenever the set of parked cars changes (the renderer's static layer rebuilds).
- `on_arrive: Callable`: Called with (car) when a vehicle reaches its goal (owner reacts), and when one is removed.

### Inner classes

- `Car`: One vehicle.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_lg: LG, p_jn: JN, p_sw: SW, seed: int) -> void`
- `func make(kind: String, role: String, dims: Vector3) -> Car`: A new vehicle (not on any lane yet).
- `func place(c: Car, l: LG.Lane, s: float) -> void`: Puts c on lane l with its front at s (registers it in the lane's sorted list).
- `func fits(l: LG.Lane, s: float, length: float) -> bool`: True when a vehicle of length `length` fits with its front at s on l (gap s0 both ways).
- `func remove(c: Car) -> void`: Removes c everywhere (lanes, slot, lists).
- `func park_at(c: Car, i: int, k: int) -> void`: Parks c in curb slot k of tile i (off the lanes).
- `func unpark(c: Car) -> bool`: Tries to pull a parked car out into the lane beside its slot. Returns true when it left.
- `func unpark_far(c: Car, fallback_tile: int) -> bool`: Takes a parked car (beyond the traffic radius) straight onto its lane as data only.
- `func rear_on(o: Car, x: LG.Lane) -> float`: Distance along lane X of o's rear when o's body covers X from behind its front lane, else -INF.
- `func point_back(c: Car, back: float) -> Vector2`: World xz of the point `back` behind c's front along its path (lane, then trail, then extrapolated).
- `func update_pose(c: Car) -> void`: Updates pos, yaw and vel from the lane state (vis_off decays separately).
- `func draw_xform(c: Car) -> Transform3D`: Drawn transform of c (with the smoothing offsets, and carried on by the time its simulation LOD has not stepped yet, never past what its last step allowed).
- `func aabb(c: Car) -> AABB`: World AABB of c (from its oriented box).
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`: Advances every vehicle by dt seconds of game-scaled time.
- `func permit(c: Car, x: LG.Lane, mv: LG.Lane, after: LG.Lane, d_stop: float) -> bool`: True when c may pass the stop point of approach x into move mv (then the lane `after`).
- `func hold_reason(c: Car, x: LG.Lane, mv: LG.Lane, after: LG.Lane, d_stop: float) -> String`: Why c must hold at the stop point of approach x ("" when it may go): red, amber, zebra, yield, box, room.
- `func why_held(c: Car) -> String`: The hold reason for c at the next stop point within reach ("" when none), for tests and tuning.
- `func make_far(c: Car) -> void`: Takes c off the lanes and keeps it moving as data.
- `func make_near(c: Car) -> bool`: Puts a data-only vehicle back on its lane when there is room. Returns true on success.
- `func begin_pull_in(c: Car, i: int, k: int) -> void`: Starts the slide from the lane into curb slot (i, k): the car must be stopped beside it.
- `func on_lanes_rebuilt(tiles: Dictionary) -> void`: Re-places vehicles on rebuilt tiles and keeps their drawn position continuous.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

People on foot (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §3 Pedestrians): they walk the sidewalk network at PED_WALK ±15 %, keep right when they meet, keep 0.6 m apart, follow slower walkers, sidestep the posts baked into lit straights, the light poles and the player, and cross only on zebras: in their walk phase at lights, or at tees when no car is within 2 s. A walker either wanders (ambient), follows a plan of network edges and free legs (resident trips), or stands (waiting, chatting, outdoors).

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `JN = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/junctions.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `BAND = (WS.PED_BAND[1] - WS.PED_BAND[0]) * 0.5 - 0.002`: Half width of the walking band around its centreline (PED_BAND).
- `SEP = 0.6 * WS.M`
- `KEEP_RIGHT = 0.012`
- `CELL = 0.06`
- `LOD_FULL = 1.5`: Simulation LOD: walkers within LOD_FULL of the player step every step, out to LOD_NEAR (the drawing range) every LOD_MID_DT, beyond that every LOD_DT without crowd logic. Draws carry them on in between.
- `LOD_MID_DT = 1.0 / 15.0`
- `LOD_NEAR = 4.6`
- `LOD_DT = 0.2`
- `FADE_IN = 1.6`: Seconds a person spawned in view takes to fade in.
- `CHATTY = 0.22`: Ambient walkers who stop to chat when they meet (a pair of them stands out of the flow).
- `CHAT_MEET = 1.3 * WS.M`
- `CHAT_MIN = 10.0`
- `CHAT_MAX = 40.0`
- `WAIT_ALONG = [0.0, -0.6, 0.6]`: People waiting at a zebra spread along the curb (metres, by slot) and step back a row. The rows behind the first stand staggered, clear of the light pole 0.8 m behind the middle of the curb.
- `WAIT_ALONG_BACK = [-0.55, 0.55, -1.15]`
- `WAIT_ROW = 0.55`
- `HIP_M = 0.91`: Hip height of the legacy people (half their 1.83 m), the pivot of the leg swing.
- `HC_SPEED = Vector2(1.15, 1.50)`: HC bodies (deliverable 9): walking speeds in m/s, and the share of walkers carrying a box or on the phone, and the idle variants.
- `CARRY = 0.10`
- `PHONE = 0.08`
- `IDLES = [&"idle", &"idle", &"idle_look", &"idle_wait"]`

### Properties

- `posts: Array[Vector2]`: Obstacles on sidewalks (the posts in lit straights): Array[Vector2].
- `hc: bool`: True when HC's animated bodies draw people (people.gd): speeds follow HC_SPEED.
- `on_removed: Callable`: Called with (walker) when one is removed (the renderer frees its node).

### Inner classes

- `Walker`: One person on foot.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sw: SW, p_lg: LG, p_jn: JN, p_vh: VH, seed: int) -> void`
- `func make(role: String) -> Walker`
- `func remove(w: Walker) -> void`
- `func place(w: Walker, e: SW.PedEdge, t: float, dir: int) -> void`: Puts w on edge e at distance t (walking direction dir).
- `func stand(w: Walker, p: Vector3, yaw: float) -> void`: Stands w at p facing yaw (outdoors, waiting, chatting).
- `func rebuild_posts(sim: CitySim) -> void`: Rebuilds the post obstacles: the posts baked into lit straights (model-local (±0.4, ∓0.2), roads.py) and the traffic-light poles at the corners of cross tiles (junctions.gd POLE_AT).
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`
- `func zebra_cars(i: int, arm: int, secs: float) -> bool`: True when a vehicle is on, or within `secs` of, the zebra across `arm` of junction tile i.
- `func start_plan(w: Walker, plan: Array) -> void`: Starts w on a plan from where it stands (first step a free leg to the network or an edge).
- `func ease_visuals(w: Walker, delta: float) -> void`: Eases the drawn stride toward the walking speed and the fade-in toward 1 (real seconds, so a paused tour still settles).
- `func draw_xform(w: Walker) -> Transform3D`: Draw transform of w: the legs and arms swing in the people shader (render.gd), and the body bobs with them, highest as the legs pass each other.
- `func draw_phase(w: Walker) -> float`: Stride phase as drawn (carried on over the time the simulation LOD has not stepped yet).
